title: For Parents
paragraph1: As a parent, you are an important part of Scouting life. Here we have gathered information about how the activities work, what your child needs to bring with them, and how you as an adult can support the corps.
paragraph2: With us, children and young people get to experience scouting for real - with nature, Lake Mälaren, boats and community as an obvious part of the adventure. The scouts get to practice cooperation, responsibility, outdoor life and seamanship in a safe environment where everyone can grow at their own pace.
paragraph3: All children and young people should feel safe in the Scouts. We work for an activity where the Scouts are seen, listened to and respected. Our leaders are non-profit committed adults and young adults who plan and implement the activity with the best interests of the Scouts in focus. The Scout course Trygga Möten (Safe Gatherings) are an important part of the work for a safe Scout environment.
growthParagraph1: In the Scouts, children and young people get to practice taking responsibility, cooperating and daring to try new things. It's not about being the best, fastest or most experienced. It's about developing together with others.
growthParagraph2: Children gradually gain more responsibility based on age and maturity. Younger scouts discover scouting through play and simple challenges. Older scouts have greater opportunities to plan, lead and take responsibility for themselves and their patrol.
growthParagraph3: As a parent, it can sometimes feel strange to see your child packing their own things, solving problems on their own, or coming home from a hike with both dirty clothes and a big smile. But that's exactly what the Scout method is all about: children grow when they get to try, practice, and succeed together.
familyParagraph1: For younger children, scouting can be something you discover together with an adult. Familjescouting (Family Scouting) is based on play, curiosity, nature experiences and community.
familyParagraph2: Here, the child participates together with a safe adult, such as a parent, grandparent, relative or other adult the child knows well. The adult is present during the activity and is responsible for their child.
familyParagraph3: Familjescouting is a great way to get to know Scouting, the Corps and other families. It is also a way for adults to discover how fun and meaningful Scouting life can be.
safetyParagraph1: As we are a sea scout troop, water is a natural part of our activities. Safety always comes first. When we have activities on or near water, we follow our procedures for sea safety. The leaders inform about what applies to each activity, for example life jackets, clothing, assembly times and whether the scout needs to be able to swim to participate. If you have questions about water experience, swimming skills or safety, you are always welcome to talk to the leaders.
safetyParagraph2: As a parent, you are welcome to contact the leaders if there is anything we need to know to ensure your child has the best possible scouting experience. This may include allergies, medications, functional variations, fear of water, social anxiety or anything else that affects the child in the group.
safetyParagraph3: The more we know, the better we can support.
